summary: The gcloud alpha storage command group supports creating buckets and viewing or editing bucket and object metadata; The gcloud alpha storage commands provide faster uploading and downloading performance than gsutil.

supporting_pages.title: Shim for Running gcloud storage \_|\_ Cloud Storage \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: To Enable Set use gcloud storage=True in the .boto config file under the [GSUtil] section: [GSUtil] use gcloud storage=True You can also set the flag for individual commands using the top-level -o flag: gsutil -o "GSUtil:use gcloud storage=True" -m cp -p file gs://bucket/obj Available Commands The gcloud storage CLI only supports a subset of gsutil commands.

Boto Configuration Configuration found in the boto file is mapped 1:1 to gcloud environment variables where appropriate. supporting_pages.title: "Transition from gsutil to gcloud storage \_|\_ Cloud Storage \_|\_ Google\
evidence_snippets: If you have scripts that rely on parsing gsutil command output, you should review and update them for the gcloud storage format before transitioning them. gcloud command equivalents All existing gsutil commands have equivalent commands in gcloud storage , with a few exceptions.
You can get a full list of the gcloud storage commands by visiting the reference documentation or by running gcloud storage --help .
Output formatting The gcloud storage and gsutil commands format their output differently.

supporting_pages.title: Troubleshooting \_|\_ Cloud Storage \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: Note: The --additional-headers flag is not available for all gcloud storage commands, such as commands working with Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies and buckets notifications commands.

Remove the empty object with the command: gcloud storage rm gs://www.example.com/dir/ You can now access http://www.example.com/dir/ and have it return that directory's index.html file instead of the empty object.
The following example shows how to set request headers for different Cloud Storage tools: Command line Use the --additional-headers flag, which is available for most commands.
